alignments.note: The ASV recasts כֹּבֶד אֶבֶן as a predication; the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate word under rule 20, headed on *heavy*.
Waw takes the *and* written for it.
נֵטֶל recast as the predicate *weighty*; the copula is gapped and none is written.
The article stands before its own word and takes the written *the* (rule 29).
Waw rendered *But*; the connective list is read off the ASV (rule 14).
Construct noun keeps only its own word; the possessive determiner goes to the possessor under rule 29.
Construct relation recast as an English possessive; the phrase's *a* is the possessor's determiner (rule 29), so both words are this noun's.
Copula joins the predicate adjective (rule 20); *heavier* carries the lexeme.
Comparative מִן → *than*; no degree adverb is written here.
Quantifying construct keeps only its own word.
Suffix rectum takes the pronoun the ASV wrote for it (rules 18, 19).

review_notes: No *of* is written between שְׁנֵי and its suffix here, so rule 19's *all of them* pattern does not arise: the ASV writes *they both* and each morpheme takes one word.
The first two lines are nominal recastings of construct chains ('weight of a stone', 'burden of the sand'); the copula in each goes to the word the ASV made the predicate.
